printed_header: Of major importance to Lunenburg, as well as every other city and town in the Commonwealth, two particular legislative enactments became effective in 1966. The first of these, Chapter 763 of the Acts of 1965, became effective February 15, 1966. Precisely, it brings into the area of municipal employment for the first time, collective bargaining between municipalities and their employees. It applies to every county city, town, and district in the Commonwealth. Excluded from its provisions elected officials, board and commission members and police. In Lunenburg, as in most other towns, our teachers have availed themselves of this new law. This law provides that municipal employees may form their own organization and through representatives of their own choosing, bargain collectively with the munic- ipality on questions of "wages, hours and other conditions of employment and to engage in other concerted activities for the purpose of collective bargaining, or other mutual aid or protection, free from actual interference, restraint or coercion. The Lunenburg teachers have selected the Lunenburg Teacher's Association as exclusive bargaining agent and, as the law provides, the Association has already met and negotiated a con- tract with our School Committee. | Robert J. Larkin Town Counsel

printed_header: The following definitions have been included inanswer to the many people who have asked what is meant by a Chapter 81 or Chapter 90 road. Chapter 81 - General law which provides for contribution by the State for maintenance of accepted town roads (at the present time the State contributes approximately $275 per mile provided that the Town contributes at least $75 per mile). Chapter 90 - General law which provides for contributions by the State and County for construction or reconstruction of Town ways provided that such ways connect the center of two towns or connect two State highways, or a State highway and another Chapter 90 road. The State contributes 50% and the County and Town 25% each. This chapter also provides for contributions by the State and County for maintenancé of roads com- structed with Chapter 90 monies. The State, County and Town each contribute one third of maintenance cost.
